hypothesis: Current access records fail to represent item-specific physical withdrawal and return
falsifiable_test: Observe consented borrowing cycles; reconcile anonymized declarations with independently checked items
measurement: Fraction of audited transactions with identity/quantity mismatch or missing verification
plausible_alternative: Participants may self-manage items accurately despite no official checks

hypothesis: Informal equipment transfers increase unknown-current-custodian cases
falsifiable_test: Track authorized scenario transfers with and without lightweight handover record
measurement: Unknown-custodian rate and time to reconstruct custody
plausible_alternative: Original team may remain responsible even when individual holder changes

hypothesis: Lack of return condition inspection contributes to late damage identification
falsifiable_test: Trial return condition check against matched no-check tasks, with voluntary users
measurement: New unusable items discovered at return; check time
plausible_alternative: Damage could be detected later even with inspection; some defects not visible

hypothesis: Damaged and usable equipment being stored together increases inadvertent unusable-item selection
falsifiable_test: Ask independent testers to select usable items from current vs tagged mock layout
measurement: Incorrect usable selection rate and retrieval time
plausible_alternative: Users may identify damage visually without labels

hypothesis: Damage reporting lacks reliable prompt notification to secretary
falsifiable_test: Observe voluntary reporting scenarios; compare current informal message vs simple structured report
measurement: Minutes/steps to notify; missing essential fields
plausible_alternative: Students may not know item is damaged at the time
decision_if_supported: Test reporting channel and owner assignment

hypothesis: Kit handover exceptions omit component-level accountability
falsifiable_test: Test pre-approved bundle checkout and component reconciliation during a staged kit exercise
plausible_alternative: Experienced captains may already keep personal counts

hypothesis: A digital workflow without low-friction interaction will prompt recording bypass
falsifiable_test: Counterbalanced prototype test across full vs streamlined logging; optional user feedback
measurement: Completion compliance, time, errors and reported friction
plausible_alternative: Extra steps may not materially affect behavior
decision_if_supported: Apply max-interaction budget; retain offline fallback

hypothesis: Current stock condition and quantity cannot be reliably reconstructed from purchase invoices alone
evidence_status: Reported limited record scope; effect unmeasured
falsifiable_test: Compare redacted purchase records to permissioned physical item census
measurement: Difference between purchased and active usable counts; unknown items
plausible_alternative: Secretary personal knowledge may be accurate
decision_if_supported: Develop asset census and reconciliation tool

hypothesis: Approval/vendor/secretary availability contribute unequally to 3–7-day repair turnaround
falsifiable_test: Construct timeline for completed real repair cases from redacted timestamps
measurement: Median days by stage and total turnaround
plausible_alternative: Parts availability or damage severity may dominate
decision_if_supported: Prioritize measured dominant delay, not app automation by default

hypothesis: Item-use instructions could reduce avoidable damage to expensive bats
falsifiable_test: Observe care knowledge; supervised protocol adherence; long-term damage data if available
measurement: Knowledge score, protocol adherence; damage only if sufficient data
plausible_alternative: Manufacturing defects/prior wear can cause breakage
decision_if_supported: Add care guidance if evidence supports and benefit outweighs effort

hypothesis: Using verification instead of key-based inference improves strict accountability
falsifiable_test: Conduct matched independent audits after current and pilot workflows
plausible_alternative: Status may become stale between updates

hypothesis: Making rack layout neater substantially lowers issue time
evidence_status: Counterevidence: users find items easily; time unmeasured
falsifiable_test: Time retrieval separately in a sample before selecting as main intervention
measurement: Retrieval seconds; guard waiting vs walking seconds
decision_if_supported: Do not prioritize storage redesign solely for speed
